chapter: First bands and brass band practice
title: Church excursions and dances played by brass bands
summary: Parker lost a job playing Monday church excursions; talk of dances, polkas, brass bands at fairgrounds, and string bands in the district.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Dad, you been to school? When you going to school?
I'm going to school every day.
So you were telling me about you lost your job driving? What? You lost your job driving to Bugaloosa?

Oh yeah, Bob. I was going to play every Monday. The man Cotton had to be hard, you know. I was stuck with the Cotton. I went over with my band. Churches would give excursions every Monday. Different churches, you know. And they would hire us.
What kind of dances did they do? What kind of dancing did people do? What kind of dancing?
We can't do dancing. Sailors do now. Slow or fast? Slow drag. Oh, they had the dance. Just like the dance now. Walford, shawty, masoka, polka. Different pieces just like the cotton now.
Nothing. Well, they danced. And the brass band would play at the dancers or not?

Yeah, the brass band would play at the dancers. Oh, I see. At the fairgrounds, they didn't use nothing but the brass bands. City Park, all over nothing but brass bands. Too many people, the string bands would be too light. Yeah.
Would they play mazookas and waltzes with the brass band? Everything like that. That's right, polka.
Get away from that. Oh, polka. Polka! Oh! Where by mom? Wait. Where huh? That was in the country? Where now?

You went down everywhere. Down here too. Did you ever play in the district? Huh? Did you play music in the district? In the district? No, I never did. I never did. I never did. What kind of music did they have there? Oh, the string and everything right now. Drummond, violin, climbing, drums, piano.
